Support · iCloud Photos

iCloud Photos downloads and scanning

Last updated November 5, 2026

LensPin can ask Apple Photos to download a photo stored only in iCloud when it needs original metadata for matching. Connection speed, file size, storage, and iOS background rules affect how long that takes.

☁

iCloud is part of the Photos request

LensPin does not connect to an independent photo cloud. Apple's Photos retrieves the photo under your iCloud configuration.

What may need to download

A thumbnail can be visible in Photos while the original file is stored only in iCloud. LensPin may need the local original to read camera and capture-time metadata that is not available from the Photos item alone.

What progress means

The scan tracks completed items and can report how many photos required iCloud retrieval. A slow item does not mean the matching engine is uploading the photo; it usually means Photos is obtaining the original.

Start with one trip

Scanning a large date range can trigger many original downloads. Try a smaller trip first to check eligibility, download progress, and matching time before expanding to a larger library. Read the public feedback about large-batch iCloud performance.

Keep enough local space

Large RAW files and iCloud downloads can require temporary local storage. If storage is low, finish other downloads, free space, or try a smaller batch. Saving a library location keeps the original unchanged. Optional JPG export creates separate copies and can require additional temporary space.

Scanning in the background

  • When background processing is available: LensPin can use system support to keep a scan you started running in the background or while the device is locked, with progress shown by the system.
  • When background time is limited: LensPin keeps the screen awake on the scan view; a long absence can pause work until you return.

If a scan appears stuck

  1. Open Photos and confirm the original can download there.
  2. Check Wi-Fi or cellular access allowed for Photos.
  3. Keep LensPin open if background scanning pauses.
  4. Try a shorter date range to identify a specific slow or unavailable photo.
  5. Preserve the progress count and any displayed error before restarting.
Do not repeatedly restart a large scan.

If Photos is still downloading originals, repeated restarts can discard useful progress. Return to LensPin first and let the current task continue when possible.

Privacy boundary

iCloud transfer is handled by Apple under your Photos settings. LensPin does not send the original to a LensPin server. Read the full privacy explanation.

Troubleshoot photo locations

Missing GPS, wrong locations or photos absent from the map
